haiku-low.q1: They see the same reply: 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: They get the same reply. Nothing is written, nothing is revoked, no email is sent, and the existing link keeps working.
haiku-low.q3: 30 minutes from issue. A newer reset link revokes it, or a successful password change uses it up.
haiku-low.q4: Still active and unchanged. The form is shown again with an error, and the link stays usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: None. All sessions are deleted, including this device. The user is redirected to /login and must log in again. A racing login may survive (open question 9).
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure without the token and drops the job. Nobody is told; the user sees the same reply.
haiku-low.q7: The email job holds the raw token and the email contains the link. The raw token stays in the queue row until the job is deleted.
haiku-low.q8: It SHA-256 hashes the URL token and looks up the row by token_hash. Found with state active and expires_at later than now shows the form; otherwise the expired page.
haiku-low.q9: In password_resets, counted as rows with user_id and issued_at within the last hour, using an index on (user_id, issued_at). Old rows fall out as time passes.
haiku-low.q10: Older active links are revoked in the same transaction that inserts the new link, only when the rate limit allows the request.
haiku-low.q11: Link marked used, password hash updated, sessions deleted, all in one transaction. The 'password changed' email job is written in that same transaction before COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: Both paths lock the users row first with FOR UPDATE, then the link row. The second waits, then finds state used and shows the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the same 200 reply as everyone: 'If an account exists for that address, we've sent a link.' Nothing is sent: no row, no email, no job.
sonnet.q2: The server sees 3 or more links issued in the last hour, commits without writing anything, and gives the same reply. No new link, no revoke, no email. The existing link keeps working.
sonnet.q3: It works for 30 minutes (expires_at = issued_at + 30 min). It can end sooner if it is used (state used), or revoked when a newer link is issued for the same user.
sonnet.q4: Still active. The form is shown again with an error and nothing is written. The link stays usable until it expires, so the user can retry.
sonnet.q5: None. All sessions rows for the user are deleted, including the current device. No session is created. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in again with the new password.
sonnet.q6: The worker retries up to 3 times with backoff, then logs the failure (without the token), deletes the job and drops it. Nobody is told. The user sees the same reply, the link expires in 30 minutes, and they may ask again, which uses another slot.
sonnet.q7: The raw token is put in the email job (queue row, or outbox row copied by the relay) written in the same transaction as the link. The worker reads it from the job and sends the email with the link. The job is deleted after a successful send.
sonnet.q8: Compute the SHA-256 of the token from the URL. Look for a password_resets row with that token_hash, state='active' and expires_at > now(). If found, show the new-password form with the token in a hidden field. If not, show the 'this link has expired, request a new one' page (the same page whether never issued, used, revoked or expired).
sonnet.q9: It is not a stored counter. It is computed with a count(*) on password_resets rows for the user_id with issued_at > now() - 1h, in any state, using the index on (user_id, issued_at). Old requests drop out as their issued_at passes the rolling hour. Rows older than 24 hours are deleted by cleanup, which the design leaves open (what runs it is not chosen).
sonnet.q10: In step 1.4, after the rate-limit check passes and the token is made, and before inserting the new row, all of the user's older active links are updated to state='revoked'. This is in the same transaction. An over-limit request revokes nothing.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: mark the link used with used_at, update users.password_hash, delete all the user's sessions rows, and write the 'password changed' email job. The job is written inside the same transaction, before COMMIT.
sonnet.q12: Step 3.4 locks the users row (FOR UPDATE) first, then the link row. The second submit waits. After the first commits, the second re-checks under the lock, finds state 'used', rolls back and shows the expired page. Only the first changes the password.
